interchanges.source: Exit ref, name and destination signs read from OpenStreetMap highway=motorway_junction nodes on a motorway or trunk way running along the leg's archived route, and the destination tags of this exit's own motorway_link ramps, OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-11-16. at_mi derived: the mean of the exit's junction nodes (one per carriageway) projected onto that route, rescaled to the leg's miles: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_far_end_source: derived: this exit's motorway_link chains walked from every gore within 500 m of its junction nodes, both carriageways, in the OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-11-16. 'motorway' means every chain merges onto a highway=motorway way; 'surface' means at least one chain ends off the motorway network: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_length_source: derived from OpenStreetMap geometry: summed node-to-node distance along this exit's motorway_link way(s), from the gore node where the ramp leaves the motorway to the nearest node where it ends (a public road -- trunk to residential, not a service or private way -- or a dead end, else a motorway merge). Per direction of travel: the gore nearest the exit's junction nodes whose first ramp edge runs that way. Starts at the OSM diverge, at or near the gore, so any deceleration lane before it is not included. Screened: under 300 ft or over 1.5 mi dropped, not clamped. OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-11-16: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_terminal_source: read from OpenStreetMap topology: the node where the same walk that measures ramp_length ends (the public crossroad or dead end the motorway_link way reaches), per direction of travel. Only baked beside a length that passed its screen, and never for a ramp that ends in a merge. OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-11-16: https://www.openstreetmap.org/

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-23. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply, and on exposed concrete built= and improved= (HPMS Year_Last_Construction and YEAR_LAST_IMPROVEMENT, READ, the year of each date; a run splits where either changes); each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.
meta.deck_source: National Bridge Inventory, NTAD feature service (Bureau of Transportation Statistics, https://services.arcgis.com/xOi1kZaI0eWDREZv/arcgis/rest/services/NTAD_National_Bridge_Inventory/FeatureServer/0), accessed 2026-11-23; codes per the FHWA Recording and Coding Guide for the Structure Inventory and Appraisal of the Nation's Bridges (1995, https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/bridge/mtguide.pdf): Item 5A record type (page 2), Item 43B structure type (page 24), Items 45, 48 and 49 spans and lengths (pages 26 to 28), Item 107 deck structure type and Item 108A wearing surface (page 70). A structure's deck= is READ: open_grating is Item 107 code 3; concrete is 107 code 1 or 2 under 108A 0 to 4; asphalt is 108A code 6; other is anything else. Which record belongs to which structure is DERIVED: a record carried on the structure whose point projects within 60 m of the archived road, inside the structure or within 0.02 mi of its ends, with an Item 49 length within 0.05 mi of the structure's measured span; the best length fit wins, then the nearer point. nbi= is the record's state FIPS and structure number. grate=from:to on a movable open grating (43B 15, 16 or 17) is DERIVED: Item 45 spans times Item 48, centred on the structure (NBI's point may be the bridge's beginning, Item 16, page 8), clipped to it. A structure with no tag matched no record.

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-22. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply, and on exposed concrete built= and improved= (HPMS Year_Last_Construction and YEAR_LAST_IMPROVEMENT, READ, the year of each date; a run splits where either changes); each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.
meta.deck_source: National Bridge Inventory, NTAD feature service (Bureau of Transportation Statistics, https://services.arcgis.com/xOi1kZaI0eWDREZv/arcgis/rest/services/NTAD_National_Bridge_Inventory/FeatureServer/0), accessed 2026-11-22; codes per the FHWA Recording and Coding Guide for the Structure Inventory and Appraisal of the Nation's Bridges (1995, https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/bridge/mtguide.pdf): Item 5A record type (page 2), Item 43B structure type (page 24), Items 45, 48 and 49 spans and lengths (pages 26 to 28), Item 107 deck structure type and Item 108A wearing surface (page 70). A structure's deck= is READ: open_grating is Item 107 code 3; concrete is 107 code 1 or 2 under 108A 0 to 4; asphalt is 108A code 6; other is anything else. Which record belongs to which structure is DERIVED: a record carried on the structure whose point projects within 60 m of the archived road, inside the structure or within 0.02 mi of its ends, with an Item 49 length within 0.05 mi of the structure's measured span; the best length fit wins, then the nearer point. nbi= is the record's state FIPS and structure number. grate=from:to on a movable open grating (43B 15, 16 or 17) is DERIVED: Item 45 spans times Item 48, centred on the structure (NBI's point may be the bridge's beginning, Item 16, page 8), clipped to it. A structure with no tag matched no record.

interchanges.source: Exit ref, name and destination signs read from OpenStreetMap highway=motorway_junction nodes on a motorway or trunk way running along the leg's archived route, and the destination tags of this exit's own motorway_link ramps, OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-11-16. at_mi derived: the mean of the exit's junction nodes (one per carriageway) projected onto that route, rescaled to the leg's miles: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_control_source: OpenStreetMap highway=traffic_signals/highway=stop/highway=give_way node within 120 m of the walked terminal node where this exit's ramp chain ends (read; the walk supplies the node, the tag supplies the control), OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-11-16: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_far_end_source: derived: this exit's motorway_link chains walked from every gore within 500 m of its junction nodes, both carriageways, in the OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-11-16. 'motorway' means every chain merges onto a highway=motorway way; 'surface' means at least one chain ends off the motorway network: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_length_source: derived from OpenStreetMap geometry: summed node-to-node distance along this exit's motorway_link way(s), from the gore node where the ramp leaves the motorway to the nearest node where it ends (a public road -- trunk to residential, not a service or private way -- or a dead end, else a motorway merge). Per direction of travel: the gore nearest the exit's junction nodes whose first ramp edge runs that way. Starts at the OSM diverge, at or near the gore, so any deceleration lane before it is not included. Screened: under 300 ft or over 1.5 mi dropped, not clamped. OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-11-16: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_terminal_source: read from OpenStreetMap topology: the node where the same walk that measures ramp_length ends (the public crossroad or dead end the motorway_link way reaches), per direction of travel. Only baked beside a length that passed its screen, and never for a ramp that ends in a merge. OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-11-16: https://www.openstreetmap.org/

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-22. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.
meta.deck_source: National Bridge Inventory, NTAD feature service (Bureau of Transportation Statistics, https://services.arcgis.com/xOi1kZaI0eWDREZv/arcgis/rest/services/NTAD_National_Bridge_Inventory/FeatureServer/0), accessed 2026-11-23; codes per the FHWA Recording and Coding Guide for the Structure Inventory and Appraisal of the Nation's Bridges (1995, https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/bridge/mtguide.pdf): Item 5A record type (page 2), Item 43B structure type (page 24), Items 45, 48 and 49 spans and lengths (pages 26 to 28), Item 107 deck structure type and Item 108A wearing surface (page 70). A structure's deck= is READ: open_grating is Item 107 code 3; concrete is 107 code 1 or 2 under 108A 0 to 4; asphalt is 108A code 6; other is anything else. Which record belongs to which structure is DERIVED: a record carried on the structure whose point projects within 60 m of the archived road, inside the structure or within 0.02 mi of its ends, with an Item 49 length within 0.05 mi of the structure's measured span; the best length fit wins, then the nearer point. nbi= is the record's state FIPS and structure number. grate=from:to on a movable open grating (43B 15, 16 or 17) is DERIVED: Item 45 spans times Item 48, centred on the structure (NBI's point may be the bridge's beginning, Item 16, page 8), clipped to it. A structure with no tag matched no record.

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-22. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply, and on exposed concrete built= and improved= (HPMS Year_Last_Construction and YEAR_LAST_IMPROVEMENT, READ, the year of each date; a run splits where either changes); each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.
meta.deck_source: National Bridge Inventory, NTAD feature service (Bureau of Transportation Statistics, https://services.arcgis.com/xOi1kZaI0eWDREZv/arcgis/rest/services/NTAD_National_Bridge_Inventory/FeatureServer/0), accessed 2026-11-22; codes per the FHWA Recording and Coding Guide for the Structure Inventory and Appraisal of the Nation's Bridges (1995, https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/bridge/mtguide.pdf): Item 5A record type (page 2), Item 43B structure type (page 24), Items 45, 48 and 49 spans and lengths (pages 26 to 28), Item 107 deck structure type and Item 108A wearing surface (page 70). A structure's deck= is READ: open_grating is Item 107 code 3; concrete is 107 code 1 or 2 under 108A 0 to 4; asphalt is 108A code 6; other is anything else. Which record belongs to which structure is DERIVED: a record carried on the structure whose point projects within 60 m of the archived road, inside the structure or within 0.02 mi of its ends, with an Item 49 length within 0.05 mi of the structure's measured span; the best length fit wins, then the nearer point. nbi= is the record's state FIPS and structure number. grate=from:to on a movable open grating (43B 15, 16 or 17) is DERIVED: Item 45 spans times Item 48, centred on the structure (NBI's point may be the bridge's beginning, Item 16, page 8), clipped to it. A structure with no tag matched no record.

The class is HPMS's own; DERIVED here only in that one value stands for a whole leg -- the modal class over the HPMS sections intersecting the leg's bounding box, since HPMS classifies sections and a leg crosses many. Accessed 2026-08-19: https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms.cfm

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-22. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply, and on exposed concrete built= and improved= (HPMS Year_Last_Construction and YEAR_LAST_IMPROVEMENT, READ, the year of each date; a run splits where either changes); each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.
meta.deck_source: National Bridge Inventory, NTAD feature service (Bureau of Transportation Statistics, https://services.arcgis.com/xOi1kZaI0eWDREZv/arcgis/rest/services/NTAD_National_Bridge_Inventory/FeatureServer/0), accessed 2026-11-22; codes per the FHWA Recording and Coding Guide for the Structure Inventory and Appraisal of the Nation's Bridges (1995, https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/bridge/mtguide.pdf): Item 5A record type (page 2), Item 43B structure type (page 24), Items 45, 48 and 49 spans and lengths (pages 26 to 28), Item 107 deck structure type and Item 108A wearing surface (page 70). A structure's deck= is READ: open_grating is Item 107 code 3; concrete is 107 code 1 or 2 under 108A 0 to 4; asphalt is 108A code 6; other is anything else. Which record belongs to which structure is DERIVED: a record carried on the structure whose point projects within 60 m of the archived road, inside the structure or within 0.02 mi of its ends, with an Item 49 length within 0.05 mi of the structure's measured span; the best length fit wins, then the nearer point. nbi= is the record's state FIPS and structure number. grate=from:to on a movable open grating (43B 15, 16 or 17) is DERIVED: Item 45 spans times Item 48, centred on the structure (NBI's point may be the bridge's beginning, Item 16, page 8), clipped to it. A structure with no tag matched no record.

interchanges.source: Exit ref, name and destination signs read from OpenStreetMap highway=motorway_junction nodes on a motorway or trunk way running along the leg's archived route, and the destination tags of this exit's own motorway_link ramps, OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-11-16. at_mi derived: the mean of the exit's junction nodes (one per carriageway) projected onto that route, rescaled to the leg's miles: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_control_source: OpenStreetMap highway=traffic_signals/highway=stop/highway=give_way node within 120 m of the walked terminal node where this exit's ramp chain ends (read; the walk supplies the node, the tag supplies the control), OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-11-16: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_far_end_source: derived: this exit's motorway_link chains walked from every gore within 500 m of its junction nodes, both carriageways, in the OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-11-16. 'motorway' means every chain merges onto a highway=motorway way; 'surface' means at least one chain ends off the motorway network: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_length_source: derived from OpenStreetMap geometry: summed node-to-node distance along this exit's motorway_link way(s), from the gore node where the ramp leaves the motorway to the nearest node where it ends (a public road -- trunk to residential, not a service or private way -- or a dead end, else a motorway merge). Per direction of travel: the gore nearest the exit's junction nodes whose first ramp edge runs that way. Starts at the OSM diverge, at or near the gore, so any deceleration lane before it is not included. Screened: under 300 ft or over 1.5 mi dropped, not clamped. OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-11-16: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_terminal_source: read from OpenStreetMap topology: the node where the same walk that measures ramp_length ends (the public crossroad or dead end the motorway_link way reaches), per direction of travel. Only baked beside a length that passed its screen, and never for a ramp that ends in a merge. OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-11-16: https://www.openstreetmap.org/

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-23. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply, and on exposed concrete built= and improved= (HPMS Year_Last_Construction and YEAR_LAST_IMPROVEMENT, READ, the year of each date; a run splits where either changes); each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.
meta.deck_source: National Bridge Inventory, NTAD feature service (Bureau of Transportation Statistics, https://services.arcgis.com/xOi1kZaI0eWDREZv/arcgis/rest/services/NTAD_National_Bridge_Inventory/FeatureServer/0), accessed 2026-11-23; codes per the FHWA Recording and Coding Guide for the Structure Inventory and Appraisal of the Nation's Bridges (1995, https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/bridge/mtguide.pdf): Item 5A record type (page 2), Item 43B structure type (page 24), Items 45, 48 and 49 spans and lengths (pages 26 to 28), Item 107 deck structure type and Item 108A wearing surface (page 70). A structure's deck= is READ: open_grating is Item 107 code 3; concrete is 107 code 1 or 2 under 108A 0 to 4; asphalt is 108A code 6; other is anything else. Which record belongs to which structure is DERIVED: a record carried on the structure whose point projects within 60 m of the archived road, inside the structure or within 0.02 mi of its ends, with an Item 49 length within 0.05 mi of the structure's measured span; the best length fit wins, then the nearer point. nbi= is the record's state FIPS and structure number. grate=from:to on a movable open grating (43B 15, 16 or 17) is DERIVED: Item 45 spans times Item 48, centred on the structure (NBI's point may be the bridge's beginning, Item 16, page 8), clipped to it. A structure with no tag matched no record.

interchanges.ramp_control_source: OpenStreetMap highway=traffic_signals/highway=stop node within 120 m of the walked terminal node where this exit's ramp chain ends (read; the walk supplies the node, the tag supplies the control), from a local Geofabrik extract, accessed 2026-06-23: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_far_end_source: derived: this exit's motorway_link chains walked from the gore in a local Geofabrik extract, accessed 2026-06-23. 'motorway' means every chain merges onto a highway=motorway way; 'surface' means at least one chain ends off the motorway network: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_length_source: derived from OpenStreetMap geometry: summed node-to-node distance along this exit's motorway_link way(s), from the gore node where the ramp leaves the motorway to the nearest node where it ends (a public road -- trunk to residential, not a service or private way -- or a dead end, else a motorway merge). Starts at the OSM diverge, at or near the gore, so any deceleration lane before it is not included; direction from the ramp's first edge against the leg. Screened: under 300 ft or over 1.5 mi dropped, not clamped. Local Geofabrik extract accessed 2026-06-23: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_terminal_source: read from OpenStreetMap topology: the node where the same walk that measures ramp_length ends (the public crossroad or dead end the motorway_link way reaches), per direction of travel. Only baked beside a length that passed its screen, and never for a ramp that ends in a merge. Local Geofabrik extract accessed 2026-06-23: https://www.openstreetmap.org/

interchanges.ramp_advisory_source: OpenStreetMap maxspeed:advisory on the motorway_link ways of this exit's ramp, per direction of travel (read; a directional suffix resolved from the way's drawn direction), the lowest on any branch of the ramp, OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_length_source: derived from OpenStreetMap geometry: summed node-to-node distance along this exit's motorway_link way(s), from the gore node where the ramp leaves the motorway to the nearest node where it ends (a public road -- trunk to residential, not a service or private way -- or a dead end, else a motorway merge). Per direction of travel: the gore nearest the exit's junction nodes whose first ramp edge runs that way. Starts at the OSM diverge, at or near the gore, so any deceleration lane before it is not included. Screened: under 300 ft or over 1.5 mi dropped, not clamped. interchanges.ramp_terminal_source: read from OpenStreetMap topology: the node where the same walk that measures ramp_length ends (the public crossroad or dead end the motorway_link way reaches), per direction of travel. interchanges.ramp_length_source: derived from OpenStreetMap geometry: summed node-to-node distance along this exit's motorway_link way(s), from the gore node where the ramp leaves the motorway to the nearest node where it ends (a public road -- trunk to residential, not a service or private way -- or a dead end, else a motorway merge). meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-22. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply, and on exposed concrete built= and improved= (HPMS Year_Last_Construction and YEAR_LAST_IMPROVEMENT, READ, the year of each date; a run splits where either changes); each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.
meta.deck_source: National Bridge Inventory, NTAD feature service (Bureau of Transportation Statistics, https://services.arcgis.com/xOi1kZaI0eWDREZv/arcgis/rest/services/NTAD_National_Bridge_Inventory/FeatureServer/0), accessed 2026-11-22; codes per the FHWA Recording and Coding Guide for the Structure Inventory and Appraisal of the Nation's Bridges (1995, https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/bridge/mtguide.pdf): Item 5A record type (page 2), Item 43B structure type (page 24), Items 45, 48 and 49 spans and lengths (pages 26 to 28), Item 107 deck structure type and Item 108A wearing surface (page 70). A structure's deck= is READ: open_grating is Item 107 code 3; concrete is 107 code 1 or 2 under 108A 0 to 4; asphalt is 108A code 6; other is anything else. Which record belongs to which structure is DERIVED: a record carried on the structure whose point projects within 60 m of the archived road, inside the structure or within 0.02 mi of its ends, with an Item 49 length within 0.05 mi of the structure's measured span; the best length fit wins, then the nearer point. nbi= is the record's state FIPS and structure number. grate=from:to on a movable open grating (43B 15, 16 or 17) is DERIVED: Item 45 spans times Item 48, centred on the structure (NBI's point may be the bridge's beginning, Item 16, page 8), clipped to it. A structure with no tag matched no record.

interchanges.source: Exit ref, name and destination signs read from OpenStreetMap highway=motorway_junction nodes on a motorway or trunk way running along the leg's archived route, and the destination tags of this exit's own motorway_link ramps, OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-11-16. at_mi derived: the mean of the exit's junction nodes (one per carriageway) projected onto that route, rescaled to the leg's miles: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_control_source: OpenStreetMap highway=traffic_signals/highway=stop/highway=give_way node within 120 m of the walked terminal node where this exit's ramp chain ends (read; the walk supplies the node, the tag supplies the control), OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-11-16: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_far_end_source: derived: this exit's motorway_link chains walked from every gore within 500 m of its junction nodes, both carriageways, in the OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-11-16. 'motorway' means every chain merges onto a highway=motorway way; 'surface' means at least one chain ends off the motorway network: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_length_source: derived from OpenStreetMap geometry: summed node-to-node distance along this exit's motorway_link way(s), from the gore node where the ramp leaves the motorway to the nearest node where it ends (a public road -- trunk to residential, not a service or private way -- or a dead end, else a motorway merge). Per direction of travel: the gore nearest the exit's junction nodes whose first ramp edge runs that way. Starts at the OSM diverge, at or near the gore, so any deceleration lane before it is not included. Screened: under 300 ft or over 1.5 mi dropped, not clamped. meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-23. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply, and on exposed concrete built= and improved= (HPMS Year_Last_Construction and YEAR_LAST_IMPROVEMENT, READ, the year of each date; a run splits where either changes); each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.
meta.deck_source: National Bridge Inventory, NTAD feature service (Bureau of Transportation Statistics, https://services.arcgis.com/xOi1kZaI0eWDREZv/arcgis/rest/services/NTAD_National_Bridge_Inventory/FeatureServer/0), accessed 2026-11-23; codes per the FHWA Recording and Coding Guide for the Structure Inventory and Appraisal of the Nation's Bridges (1995, https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/bridge/mtguide.pdf): Item 5A record type (page 2), Item 43B structure type (page 24), Items 45, 48 and 49 spans and lengths (pages 26 to 28), Item 107 deck structure type and Item 108A wearing surface (page 70). A structure's deck= is READ: open_grating is Item 107 code 3; concrete is 107 code 1 or 2 under 108A 0 to 4; asphalt is 108A code 6; other is anything else. Which record belongs to which structure is DERIVED: a record carried on the structure whose point projects within 60 m of the archived road, inside the structure or within 0.02 mi of its ends, with an Item 49 length within 0.05 mi of the structure's measured span; the best length fit wins, then the nearer point. nbi= is the record's state FIPS and structure number. grate=from:to on a movable open grating (43B 15, 16 or 17) is DERIVED: Item 45 spans times Item 48, centred on the structure (NBI's point may be the bridge's beginning, Item 16, page 8), clipped to it. A structure with no tag matched no record.

crossings.hazmat_text: Explosives and flammable tank loads may not use the San Francisco-Oakland Bay Bridge.
crossings.basis: Read: Interstate 80 on the San Francisco-Oakland Bay Bridge prohibits Division 1.1 to 1.3 explosives and hazardous materials in tank vehicles requiring flammable placards (California Highway Patrol route list; 21 CCR 1402.1). Derived: the legs are the ones whose archived road geometry runs through the Yerba Buena Island tunnel within 60 metres. Classes: each load names its 49 CFR 172.101 class, so only Division 1.1 to 1.3 explosives, and flammable gas or liquid in a tank, are refused; a load with no class (an old save) matches no class rule.

interchanges.source: Exit ref, name and destination signs read from OpenStreetMap highway=motorway_junction nodes on a motorway or trunk way running along the leg's archived route, and the destination tags of this exit's own motorway_link ramps, OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19. at_mi derived: the mean of the exit's junction nodes (one per carriageway) projected onto that route, rescaled to the leg's miles: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_far_end_source: derived: this exit's motorway_link chains walked from every gore within 500 m of its junction nodes, both carriageways, in the OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19. 'motorway' means every chain merges onto a highway=motorway way; 'surface' means at least one chain ends off the motorway network: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_advisory_source: OpenStreetMap maxspeed:advisory on the motorway_link ways of this exit's ramp, per direction of travel (read; a directional suffix resolved from the way's drawn direction), the lowest on any branch of the ramp, OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_length_source: derived from OpenStreetMap geometry: summed node-to-node distance along this exit's motorway_link way(s), from the gore node where the ramp leaves the motorway to the nearest node where it ends (a public road -- trunk to residential, not a service or private way -- or a dead end, else a motorway merge). Per direction of travel: the gore nearest the exit's junction nodes whose first ramp edge runs that way. Starts at the OSM diverge, at or near the gore, so any deceleration lane before it is not included. Screened: under 300 ft or over 1.5 mi dropped, not clamped. OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19: https://www.openstreetmap.org/

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-22. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply, and on exposed concrete built= and improved= (HPMS Year_Last_Construction and YEAR_LAST_IMPROVEMENT, READ, the year of each date; a run splits where either changes); each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.
meta.deck_source: National Bridge Inventory, NTAD feature service (Bureau of Transportation Statistics, https://services.arcgis.com/xOi1kZaI0eWDREZv/arcgis/rest/services/NTAD_National_Bridge_Inventory/FeatureServer/0), accessed 2026-11-22; codes per the FHWA Recording and Coding Guide for the Structure Inventory and Appraisal of the Nation's Bridges (1995, https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/bridge/mtguide.pdf): Item 5A record type (page 2), Item 43B structure type (page 24), Items 45, 48 and 49 spans and lengths (pages 26 to 28), Item 107 deck structure type and Item 108A wearing surface (page 70). A structure's deck= is READ: open_grating is Item 107 code 3; concrete is 107 code 1 or 2 under 108A 0 to 4; asphalt is 108A code 6; other is anything else. Which record belongs to which structure is DERIVED: a record carried on the structure whose point projects within 60 m of the archived road, inside the structure or within 0.02 mi of its ends, with an Item 49 length within 0.05 mi of the structure's measured span; the best length fit wins, then the nearer point. nbi= is the record's state FIPS and structure number. grate=from:to on a movable open grating (43B 15, 16 or 17) is DERIVED: Item 45 spans times Item 48, centred on the structure (NBI's point may be the bridge's beginning, Item 16, page 8), clipped to it. A structure with no tag matched no record.

interchanges.ramp_far_end_source: derived: this exit's motorway_link chains walked from every gore within 500 m of its junction nodes, both carriageways, in the OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-11-16. 'motorway' means every chain merges onto a highway=motorway way; 'surface' means at least one chain ends off the motorway network: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_length_source: derived from OpenStreetMap geometry: summed node-to-node distance along this exit's motorway_link way(s), from the gore node where the ramp leaves the motorway to the nearest node where it ends (a public road -- trunk to residential, not a service or private way -- or a dead end, else a motorway merge). Per direction of travel: the gore nearest the exit's junction nodes whose first ramp edge runs that way. Starts at the OSM diverge, at or near the gore, so any deceleration lane before it is not included. Screened: under 300 ft or over 1.5 mi dropped, not clamped. OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-11-16: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_terminal_source: read from OpenStreetMap topology: the node where the same walk that measures ramp_length ends (the public crossroad or dead end the motorway_link way reaches), per direction of travel. Only baked beside a length that passed its screen, and never for a ramp that ends in a merge. OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-11-16: https://www.openstreetmap.org/

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-23. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply, and on exposed concrete built= and improved= (HPMS Year_Last_Construction and YEAR_LAST_IMPROVEMENT, READ, the year of each date; a run splits where either changes); each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.
meta.deck_source: National Bridge Inventory, NTAD feature service (Bureau of Transportation Statistics, https://services.arcgis.com/xOi1kZaI0eWDREZv/arcgis/rest/services/NTAD_National_Bridge_Inventory/FeatureServer/0), accessed 2026-11-23; codes per the FHWA Recording and Coding Guide for the Structure Inventory and Appraisal of the Nation's Bridges (1995, https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/bridge/mtguide.pdf): Item 5A record type (page 2), Item 43B structure type (page 24), Items 45, 48 and 49 spans and lengths (pages 26 to 28), Item 107 deck structure type and Item 108A wearing surface (page 70). A structure's deck= is READ: open_grating is Item 107 code 3; concrete is 107 code 1 or 2 under 108A 0 to 4; asphalt is 108A code 6; other is anything else. Which record belongs to which structure is DERIVED: a record carried on the structure whose point projects within 60 m of the archived road, inside the structure or within 0.02 mi of its ends, with an Item 49 length within 0.05 mi of the structure's measured span; the best length fit wins, then the nearer point. nbi= is the record's state FIPS and structure number. grate=from:to on a movable open grating (43B 15, 16 or 17) is DERIVED: Item 45 spans times Item 48, centred on the structure (NBI's point may be the bridge's beginning, Item 16, page 8), clipped to it. A structure with no tag matched no record.

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-22. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply, and on exposed concrete built= and improved= (HPMS Year_Last_Construction and YEAR_LAST_IMPROVEMENT, READ, the year of each date; a run splits where either changes); each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.
meta.deck_source: National Bridge Inventory, NTAD feature service (Bureau of Transportation Statistics, https://services.arcgis.com/xOi1kZaI0eWDREZv/arcgis/rest/services/NTAD_National_Bridge_Inventory/FeatureServer/0), accessed 2026-11-22; codes per the FHWA Recording and Coding Guide for the Structure Inventory and Appraisal of the Nation's Bridges (1995, https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/bridge/mtguide.pdf): Item 5A record type (page 2), Item 43B structure type (page 24), Items 45, 48 and 49 spans and lengths (pages 26 to 28), Item 107 deck structure type and Item 108A wearing surface (page 70). A structure's deck= is READ: open_grating is Item 107 code 3; concrete is 107 code 1 or 2 under 108A 0 to 4; asphalt is 108A code 6; other is anything else. Which record belongs to which structure is DERIVED: a record carried on the structure whose point projects within 60 m of the archived road, inside the structure or within 0.02 mi of its ends, with an Item 49 length within 0.05 mi of the structure's measured span; the best length fit wins, then the nearer point. nbi= is the record's state FIPS and structure number. grate=from:to on a movable open grating (43B 15, 16 or 17) is DERIVED: Item 45 spans times Item 48, centred on the structure (NBI's point may be the bridge's beginning, Item 16, page 8), clipped to it. A structure with no tag matched no record.

interchanges.source: Exit ref, name and destination signs read from OpenStreetMap highway=motorway_junction nodes on a motorway or trunk way running along the leg's archived route, and the destination tags of this exit's own motorway_link ramps, OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-11-16. at_mi derived: the mean of the exit's junction nodes (one per carriageway) projected onto that route, rescaled to the leg's miles: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_control_source: OpenStreetMap highway=traffic_signals/highway=stop/highway=give_way node within 120 m of the walked terminal node where this exit's ramp chain ends (read; the walk supplies the node, the tag supplies the control), OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-11-16: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_far_end_source: derived: this exit's motorway_link chains walked from every gore within 500 m of its junction nodes, both carriageways, in the OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-11-16. 'motorway' means every chain merges onto a highway=motorway way; 'surface' means at least one chain ends off the motorway network: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_length_source: derived from OpenStreetMap geometry: summed node-to-node distance along this exit's motorway_link way(s), from the gore node where the ramp leaves the motorway to the nearest node where it ends (a public road -- trunk to residential, not a service or private way -- or a dead end, else a motorway merge). Per direction of travel: the gore nearest the exit's junction nodes whose first ramp edge runs that way. Starts at the OSM diverge, at or near the gore, so any deceleration lane before it is not included. Screened: under 300 ft or over 1.5 mi dropped, not clamped. OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-11-16: https://www.openstreetmap.org/

hpms_terrain.name: level
hpms_terrain.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Terrain_Type, read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view). The class is HPMS's own; DERIVED here only in that one value stands for a whole leg -- the modal class over the HPMS sections intersecting the leg's bounding box, since HPMS classifies sections and a leg crosses many. Accessed 2026-11-22: https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms.cfm

traffic_aadt.source: Derived from FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) AADT and through-lane counts: median of HPMS sections snapping within 250 m of a 5-mile window of the leg, rounded to the nearest 500, lone dips between agreeing neighbours carried across. Sections queried from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view) and snapped to checked-in route geometry, accessed 2026-11-22: https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms.cfm

interchanges.ramp_length_source: derived from OpenStreetMap geometry: summed node-to-node distance along this exit's motorway_link way(s), from the gore node where the ramp leaves the motorway to the nearest node where it ends (a public road -- trunk to residential, not a service or private way -- or a dead end, else a motorway merge). Per direction of travel: the gore nearest the exit's junction nodes whose first ramp edge runs that way. Starts at the OSM diverge, at or near the gore, so any deceleration lane before it is not included. Screened: under 300 ft or over 1.5 mi dropped, not clamped. OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_terminal_source: read from OpenStreetMap topology: the node where the same walk that measures ramp_length ends (the public crossroad or dead end the motorway_link way reaches), per direction of travel. Only baked beside a length that passed its screen, and never for a ramp that ends in a merge. OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19: https://www.openstreetmap.org/

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-20. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.
meta.deck_source: National Bridge Inventory, NTAD feature service (Bureau of Transportation Statistics, https://services.arcgis.com/xOi1kZaI0eWDREZv/arcgis/rest/services/NTAD_National_Bridge_Inventory/FeatureServer/0), accessed 2026-11-22; codes per the FHWA Recording and Coding Guide for the Structure Inventory and Appraisal of the Nation's Bridges (1995, https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/bridge/mtguide.pdf): Item 5A record type (page 2), Item 43B structure type (page 24), Items 45, 48 and 49 spans and lengths (pages 26 to 28), Item 107 deck structure type and Item 108A wearing surface (page 70). A structure's deck= is READ: open_grating is Item 107 code 3; concrete is 107 code 1 or 2 under 108A 0 to 4; asphalt is 108A code 6; other is anything else. Which record belongs to which structure is DERIVED: a record carried on the structure whose point projects within 60 m of the archived road, inside the structure or within 0.02 mi of its ends, with an Item 49 length within 0.05 mi of the structure's measured span; the best length fit wins, then the nearer point. nbi= is the record's state FIPS and structure number. grate=from:to on a movable open grating (43B 15, 16 or 17) is DERIVED: Item 45 spans times Item 48, centred on the structure (NBI's point may be the bridge's beginning, Item 16, page 8), clipped to it. A structure with no tag matched no record.

interchanges.source: Exit ref, name and destination signs read from OpenStreetMap highway=motorway_junction nodes on a motorway or trunk way running along the leg's archived route, and the destination tags of this exit's own motorway_link ramps, OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-11-16. at_mi derived: the mean of the exit's junction nodes (one per carriageway) projected onto that route, rescaled to the leg's miles: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_control_source: OpenStreetMap highway=traffic_signals/highway=stop/highway=give_way node within 120 m of the walked terminal node where this exit's ramp chain ends (read; the walk supplies the node, the tag supplies the control), OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-11-16: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_far_end_source: derived: this exit's motorway_link chains walked from every gore within 500 m of its junction nodes, both carriageways, in the OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-11-16. 'motorway' means every chain merges onto a highway=motorway way; 'surface' means at least one chain ends off the motorway network: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_advisory_source: OpenStreetMap maxspeed:advisory on the motorway_link ways of this exit's ramp, per direction of travel (read; a directional suffix resolved from the way's drawn direction), the lowest on any branch of the ramp, OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-11-16: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_length_source: derived from OpenStreetMap geometry: summed node-to-node distance along this exit's motorway_link way(s), from the gore node where the ramp leaves the motorway to the nearest node where it ends (a public road -- trunk to residential, not a service or private way -- or a dead end, else a motorway merge). Per direction of travel: the gore nearest the exit's junction nodes whose first ramp edge runs that way. Starts at the OSM diverge, at or near the gore, so any deceleration lane before it is not included. Screened: under 300 ft or over 1.5 mi dropped, not clamped. OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-11-16: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_terminal_source: read from OpenStreetMap topology: the node where the same walk that measures ramp_length ends (the public crossroad or dead end the motorway_link way reaches), per direction of travel. Only baked beside a length that passed its screen, and never for a ramp that ends in a merge. OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-11-16: https://www.openstreetmap.org/

hpms_terrain.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Terrain_Type, read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view). The class is HPMS's own; DERIVED here only in that one value stands for a whole leg -- the modal class over the HPMS sections intersecting the leg's bounding box, since HPMS classifies sections and a leg crosses many. Accessed 2026-11-22: https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms.cfm

traffic_aadt.source: Derived from FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) AADT and through-lane counts: median of HPMS sections snapping within 250 m of a 5-mile window of the leg, rounded to the nearest 500, lone dips between agreeing neighbours carried across. Sections queried from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view) and snapped to checked-in route geometry, accessed 2026-11-22: https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms.cfm

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-23. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply, and on exposed concrete built= and improved= (HPMS Year_Last_Construction and YEAR_LAST_IMPROVEMENT, READ, the year of each date; a run splits where either changes); each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.
meta.deck_source: National Bridge Inventory, NTAD feature service (Bureau of Transportation Statistics, https://services.arcgis.com/xOi1kZaI0eWDREZv/arcgis/rest/services/NTAD_National_Bridge_Inventory/FeatureServer/0), accessed 2026-11-23; codes per the FHWA Recording and Coding Guide for the Structure Inventory and Appraisal of the Nation's Bridges (1995, https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/bridge/mtguide.pdf): Item 5A record type (page 2), Item 43B structure type (page 24), Items 45, 48 and 49 spans and lengths (pages 26 to 28), Item 107 deck structure type and Item 108A wearing surface (page 70). A structure's deck= is READ: open_grating is Item 107 code 3; concrete is 107 code 1 or 2 under 108A 0 to 4; asphalt is 108A code 6; other is anything else. Which record belongs to which structure is DERIVED: a record carried on the structure whose point projects within 60 m of the archived road, inside the structure or within 0.02 mi of its ends, with an Item 49 length within 0.05 mi of the structure's measured span; the best length fit wins, then the nearer point. nbi= is the record's state FIPS and structure number. grate=from:to on a movable open grating (43B 15, 16 or 17) is DERIVED: Item 45 spans times Item 48, centred on the structure (NBI's point may be the bridge's beginning, Item 16, page 8), clipped to it. A structure with no tag matched no record.

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-22. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply, and on exposed concrete built= and improved= (HPMS Year_Last_Construction and YEAR_LAST_IMPROVEMENT, READ, the year of each date; a run splits where either changes); each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.
meta.deck_source: National Bridge Inventory, NTAD feature service (Bureau of Transportation Statistics, https://services.arcgis.com/xOi1kZaI0eWDREZv/arcgis/rest/services/NTAD_National_Bridge_Inventory/FeatureServer/0), accessed 2026-11-22; codes per the FHWA Recording and Coding Guide for the Structure Inventory and Appraisal of the Nation's Bridges (1995, https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/bridge/mtguide.pdf): Item 5A record type (page 2), Item 43B structure type (page 24), Items 45, 48 and 49 spans and lengths (pages 26 to 28), Item 107 deck structure type and Item 108A wearing surface (page 70). A structure's deck= is READ: open_grating is Item 107 code 3; concrete is 107 code 1 or 2 under 108A 0 to 4; asphalt is 108A code 6; other is anything else. Which record belongs to which structure is DERIVED: a record carried on the structure whose point projects within 60 m of the archived road, inside the structure or within 0.02 mi of its ends, with an Item 49 length within 0.05 mi of the structure's measured span; the best length fit wins, then the nearer point. nbi= is the record's state FIPS and structure number. grate=from:to on a movable open grating (43B 15, 16 or 17) is DERIVED: Item 45 spans times Item 48, centred on the structure (NBI's point may be the bridge's beginning, Item 16, page 8), clipped to it. A structure with no tag matched no record.

landmarks.name: Palm Springs Aerial Tramway (eastbound)
landmarks.spoken: Billboard: The Palm Springs Aerial Tramway, ahead. Its cars rotate all the way up the cliffs, almost six thousand feet. The view comes around to you.

landmarks.name: Cabazon Dinosaurs
landmarks.spoken: Billboard: Giant dinosaurs ahead at Cabazon. A brontosaurus with a gift shop in its belly and a tyrannosaurus glaring at the freeway. You have seen them in the movies, experience them today.

landmarks.name: Cabazon Dinosaurs (westbound)

landmarks.name: San Gorgonio Windmills

interchanges.source: OpenStreetMap highway=motorway_junction exit ref and destination sign tags on the leg's Interstate shield, snapped to checked-in OSRM route geometry, accessed 2026-06-23: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_control_source: OpenStreetMap highway=traffic_signals/highway=stop node within 120 m of the walked terminal node where this exit's ramp chain ends (read; the walk supplies the node, the tag supplies the control), from a local Geofabrik extract, accessed 2026-06-23: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_far_end_source: derived: this exit's motorway_link chains walked from the gore in a local Geofabrik extract, accessed 2026-06-23. 'motorway' means every chain merges onto a highway=motorway way; 'surface' means at least one chain ends off the motorway network: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_advisory_source: OpenStreetMap maxspeed:advisory on the motorway_link way at this exit (read; directional suffix resolved from OSM way direction into leg direction), from a local Geofabrik extract, accessed 2026-06-23: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_length_source: derived from OpenStreetMap geometry: summed node-to-node distance along this exit's motorway_link way(s), from the gore node where the ramp leaves the motorway to the nearest node where it ends (a public road -- trunk to residential, not a service or private way -- or a dead end, else a motorway merge). Starts at the OSM diverge, at or near the gore, so any deceleration lane before it is not included; direction from the ramp's first edge against the leg. Screened: under 300 ft or over 1.5 mi dropped, not clamped. Local Geofabrik extract accessed 2026-06-23: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_terminal_source: read from OpenStreetMap topology: the node where the same walk that measures ramp_length ends (the public crossroad or dead end the motorway_link way reaches), per direction of travel. Only baked beside a length that passed its screen, and never for a ramp that ends in a merge. Local Geofabrik extract accessed 2026-06-23: https://www.openstreetmap.org/

interchanges.source: Exit ref, name and destination signs read from OpenStreetMap highway=motorway_junction nodes on a motorway or trunk way running along the leg's archived route, and the destination tags of this exit's own motorway_link ramps, OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19. at_mi derived: the mean of the exit's junction nodes (one per carriageway) projected onto that route, rescaled to the leg's miles: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_control_source: OpenStreetMap highway=traffic_signals/highway=stop/highway=give_way node within 120 m of the walked terminal node where this exit's ramp chain ends (read; the walk supplies the node, the tag supplies the control), OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_far_end_source: derived: this exit's motorway_link chains walked from every gore within 500 m of its junction nodes, both carriageways, in the OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19. 'motorway' means every chain merges onto a highway=motorway way; 'surface' means at least one chain ends off the motorway network: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_advisory_source: OpenStreetMap maxspeed:advisory on the motorway_link ways of this exit's ramp, per direction of travel (read; a directional suffix resolved from the way's drawn direction), the lowest on any branch of the ramp, OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_length_source: derived from OpenStreetMap geometry: summed node-to-node distance along this exit's motorway_link way(s), from the gore node where the ramp leaves the motorway to the nearest node where it ends (a public road -- trunk to residential, not a service or private way -- or a dead end, else a motorway merge). Per direction of travel: the gore nearest the exit's junction nodes whose first ramp edge runs that way. Starts at the OSM diverge, at or near the gore, so any deceleration lane before it is not included. Screened: under 300 ft or over 1.5 mi dropped, not clamped. OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19: https://www.openstreetmap.org/

hpms_terrain.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Terrain_Type, read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view). The class is HPMS's own; DERIVED here only in that one value stands for a whole leg -- the modal class over the HPMS sections intersecting the leg's bounding box, since HPMS classifies sections and a leg crosses many. Accessed 2026-08-19: https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms.cfm

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-22. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply, and on exposed concrete built= and improved= (HPMS Year_Last_Construction and YEAR_LAST_IMPROVEMENT, READ, the year of each date; a run splits where either changes); each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.
meta.deck_source: National Bridge Inventory, NTAD feature service (Bureau of Transportation Statistics, https://services.arcgis.com/xOi1kZaI0eWDREZv/arcgis/rest/services/NTAD_National_Bridge_Inventory/FeatureServer/0), accessed 2026-11-22; codes per the FHWA Recording and Coding Guide for the Structure Inventory and Appraisal of the Nation's Bridges (1995, https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/bridge/mtguide.pdf): Item 5A record type (page 2), Item 43B structure type (page 24), Items 45, 48 and 49 spans and lengths (pages 26 to 28), Item 107 deck structure type and Item 108A wearing surface (page 70). A structure's deck= is READ: open_grating is Item 107 code 3; concrete is 107 code 1 or 2 under 108A 0 to 4; asphalt is 108A code 6; other is anything else. Which record belongs to which structure is DERIVED: a record carried on the structure whose point projects within 60 m of the archived road, inside the structure or within 0.02 mi of its ends, with an Item 49 length within 0.05 mi of the structure's measured span; the best length fit wins, then the nearer point. nbi= is the record's state FIPS and structure number. grate=from:to on a movable open grating (43B 15, 16 or 17) is DERIVED: Item 45 spans times Item 48, centred on the structure (NBI's point may be the bridge's beginning, Item 16, page 8), clipped to it. A structure with no tag matched no record.

interchanges.ramp_far_end_source: derived: this exit's motorway_link chains walked from every gore within 500 m of its junction nodes, both carriageways, in the OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19. 'motorway' means every chain merges onto a highway=motorway way; 'surface' means at least one chain ends off the motorway network: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_length_source: derived from OpenStreetMap geometry: summed node-to-node distance along this exit's motorway_link way(s), from the gore node where the ramp leaves the motorway to the nearest node where it ends (a public road -- trunk to residential, not a service or private way -- or a dead end, else a motorway merge). Per direction of travel: the gore nearest the exit's junction nodes whose first ramp edge runs that way. Starts at the OSM diverge, at or near the gore, so any deceleration lane before it is not included. Screened: under 300 ft or over 1.5 mi dropped, not clamped. OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_terminal_source: read from OpenStreetMap topology: the node where the same walk that measures ramp_length ends (the public crossroad or dead end the motorway_link way reaches), per direction of travel. Only baked beside a length that passed its screen, and never for a ramp that ends in a merge. OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19: https://www.openstreetmap.org/

Starts at the OSM diverge, at or near the gore, so any deceleration lane before it is not included. Screened: under 300 ft or over 1.5 mi dropped, not clamped. OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_terminal_source: read from OpenStreetMap topology: the node where the same walk that measures ramp_length ends (the public crossroad or dead end the motorway_link way reaches), per direction of travel. Only baked beside a length that passed its screen, and never for a ramp that ends in a merge. OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19: https://www.openstreetmap.org/

interchanges.ramp_far_end_source: derived: this exit's motorway_link chains walked from every gore within 500 m of its junction nodes, both carriageways, in the OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19. 'motorway' means every chain merges onto a highway=motorway way; 'surface' means at least one chain ends off the motorway network: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_length_source: derived from OpenStreetMap geometry: summed node-to-node distance along this exit's motorway_link way(s), from the gore node where the ramp leaves the motorway to the nearest node where it ends (a public road -- trunk to residential, not a service or private way -- or a dead end, else a motorway merge). Per direction of travel: the gore nearest the exit's junction nodes whose first ramp edge runs that way. Starts at the OSM diverge, at or near the gore, so any deceleration lane before it is not included. Screened: under 300 ft or over 1.5 mi dropped, not clamped. OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19: https://www.openstreetmap.org/

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-22. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply, and on exposed concrete built= and improved= (HPMS Year_Last_Construction and YEAR_LAST_IMPROVEMENT, READ, the year of each date; a run splits where either changes); each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.
meta.deck_source: National Bridge Inventory, NTAD feature service (Bureau of Transportation Statistics, https://services.arcgis.com/xOi1kZaI0eWDREZv/arcgis/rest/services/NTAD_National_Bridge_Inventory/FeatureServer/0), accessed 2026-11-22; codes per the FHWA Recording and Coding Guide for the Structure Inventory and Appraisal of the Nation's Bridges (1995, https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/bridge/mtguide.pdf): Item 5A record type (page 2), Item 43B structure type (page 24), Items 45, 48 and 49 spans and lengths (pages 26 to 28), Item 107 deck structure type and Item 108A wearing surface (page 70). A structure's deck= is READ: open_grating is Item 107 code 3; concrete is 107 code 1 or 2 under 108A 0 to 4; asphalt is 108A code 6; other is anything else. Which record belongs to which structure is DERIVED: a record carried on the structure whose point projects within 60 m of the archived road, inside the structure or within 0.02 mi of its ends, with an Item 49 length within 0.05 mi of the structure's measured span; the best length fit wins, then the nearer point. nbi= is the record's state FIPS and structure number. grate=from:to on a movable open grating (43B 15, 16 or 17) is DERIVED: Item 45 spans times Item 48, centred on the structure (NBI's point may be the bridge's beginning, Item 16, page 8), clipped to it.
